claims.text: The starting material is nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11.
The nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 starting material can be produced by conventional powder-metallurgy routes.
A pre-consolidation coating can homogeneously distribute 5–20 nm Y2O3 nanoparticles over the alloy powder.
After consolidation, the Y2O3 nanoparticles will be uniformly distributed at grain boundaries and within grains.
The dispersed Y2O3 particles will act as sinks for irradiation-generated vacancies and interstitials.
The dispersed Y2O3 particles will act as microstructural pinning sites.
Absorption of irradiation-generated point defects by Y2O3 particles will reduce radiation-induced solute segregation.
Reduced solute segregation will reduce nucleation of radiation-induced precipitates.
Y2O3 dispersion will stabilize grain boundaries in nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11.
Y2O3-induced grain-boundary stability will improve sintering and densification.
At approximately 8 dpa and 500°C, Y2O3-modified W38Ta36Cr15V11 will have a lower volume fraction of radiation-induced precipitates than the unmodified alloy.
At approximately 8 dpa and 500°C, Y2O3-modified W38Ta36Cr15V11 will retain negligible irradiation hardening.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will show improved microstructural stability and bulk consolidation relative to the unmodified alloy.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 develops radiation-induced precipitation after irradiation to approximately 8 dpa at 500°C.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits negligible irradiation hardening under approximately 8 dpa irradiation at 500°C.
The proposed intervention is applicable near 500°C and at irradiation doses on the order of 8 dpa.
